When Israel entered and conquered the promised land Yahweh gave certain parts of it to each tribe and family. These parts were always to stay in that family. Sometimes families had to sell parts of that land because of debt or other poverty. But, except for certain circumstances, that land always had to go back to the original family in the 50th year. Because this is all discussed later in the chapter, there is no need to include this extra information here.

36.note: Here, fearing God is given as the reason for not charging interest and letting your brother live with you. If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since the second phrase gives the reason for the result the first phrase describes. Alternate translation: [Because you must fear your God, you shall not take interest or profit from him, and your brother shall live with you] or [Since you must honor your God, do not charge him interest or profit, and let your brother live with you]

37.note: Here the verse expresses a single idea by repeating it in a way that the middle parts match (**interest** and **profit**) and the outside parts (**silver** and **food**) match. The two parts emphasize that you should not profit from lending anything to a poor person. If your language has a natural way to express this kind of emphasis through repetition, you could use it. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine the ideas and express the emphasis in another way. Alternate translation: [Do not charge interest when you lend money or food to him] or [You must not make any profit when you lend either silver or food to him]
